title: Housekeeping: Stewards Can't Cover Trays, Cleaning and Cabins

fields.subject: Steward coverage tonight: I need a decision on what gives
fields.body:
Hotel Director,

I wrote this at 23:50 and held it to attach the 24:00 count.

To keep the public areas on the 2-hour cycle, I have pulled 46 cabin stewards off cabin turns. About 210 cabins in the aft sections got no evening turndown. The 40-steward isolation meal routes are running 35 to 50 minutes late because the same supervisors run both.

Two stewards were told to deliver trays and then do a chlorine wipe-down in the next corridor. I have stopped that.

The chlorine mixing station is making 1,000 ppm, though its dosing pump has faulted twice this week and been reset by the night engineer (maintenance log: pump seal replaced 14 Feb, 'intermittent low flow' alarm cleared twice), and we are using gowns faster than planned.

The 24:00 log shows 52 passenger cases. If the count keeps rising tonight, I can't cover isolation trays, the 2-hour cycle and the cabins all at once. I need a decision on what gives.
fields.signature:
Housekeeper
Executive Housekeeper | MV Halcyon Dawn
Halcyon Reach Cruises

instructorNote: This tests whether the Hotel Director spells out the steward trade-off between tray routes, the public-area cleaning cycle and cabin turns. Watch whether the Hotel Director keeps tray delivery and cleaning strictly separate and reprioritizes before isolation meals slip. Also watch whether VP Fleet Operations treats the 52-case trend (1.7% of 2,980), the steward limit and gown use as early inputs for the Sunday turnaround.
